_comment: Military balancing. territory: radius of the land an occupied building claims, in the round hex metric of PathFinder.InCircle. Measured from the original maps' owner bytes (edge of the land around the buildings: tower 931, big tower 967, castle 1101 = radius squared), so the values reproduce the original.
_soldiersComment: Homestead's own combat values. damage per hit, one hit every attackSeconds; bowmen shoot up to range fields (also from the tower). Level 2/3 multiply health and damage by levelBonus.
_doorComment: Attacked military buildings: melee attackers first break the door (as much health as a level-1 soldier of type healthOf). With no enemy within calmRadius fields of the door fight for calmSeconds, the guard goes back in and the door repairs itself evenly, from broken to whole in regenSeconds (half after 15 s); already its first moment of repair takes another hit to break it. fighters: how many melee attackers fit at the door at once (fields next to it; pikemen too, bowmen not at all), per building name, 2 elsewhere.

door._pointsComment: Where a door fight takes place, per people and building, as grid offsets [x, y] from the door: guard = where the defender stands, fighters = where melee attackers fight it (the first 'fighters' of them are used). One step in x is 16 px to the right on screen, one step in y 9 px down and 8 px to the left; lower fields are drawn in front of the building. Buildings missing here (or with a field that is not walkable on the spot) get fields found automatically.

_hospitalComment: Hospital: its healer calls the nearest wounded own idle soldier within callRadius fields of the door to the field in front of it. Whenever a wounded own soldier stands still at the door, the healer comes out, heals it fully in healSeconds and goes back in; after a heal it waits callPauseSeconds before calling the next one (soldiers that come by themselves are healed at once).
_geologistHealthComment: Geologists of other players are fought like soldiers (they do not strike back) and have this much health.
_scoutsComment: Scouts look like a carrier of their own to other players. An enemy soldier outside the buildings within revealRadius fields sees through it, a computer player as soon as the scout is on its land; only then is he fought (health as for geologists, he does not strike back). sight: radius he sees in the fog of war (a settler sees 8). Stealing, he takes the nearest good of somebody else within stealRadius fields, one unit, and walks at loadedSpeed times his speed until he stands still on his own land, where he drops it (also where he dies).
_buildingSightComment: Fog of war: finished own buildings of these names reveal their surroundings up to this radius (other buildings only through land and settlers).
_combatPathRadiusComment: Near the enemy, soldiers plan their way within this radius around everyone standing (own soldiers too).
_combatStrengthComment: Combat strength (Kampfkraft) like the original: on own land a soldier always hits with 100 %. Elsewhere (neutral or enemy land) it starts at 100 % / number of players; goods lying on the player's own land raise it, at most to 100 %. goods: what a unit counts (per people in civilizations: Egyptians get half from gold and double from gems). The rise gets dearer: each stepPercent points of bonus cost unitsPerPercent[i] units per point (the first 10 points 1 unit each, the next 10 points 1.5 each, ...; the last value goes on). Two players need 115 gold bars for 100 % (Egyptians 230 bars or 57.5 gems).
